idiom_name: Optional + ?? at the boundary; protocol extension default implementations
implementation_notes: Swift handles absence with Optional and the nil-coalescing operator, so a factory usually returns a non-optional value by composing `found ?? .unknown`; for collaborators, a protocol extension supplies the benign bodies for a conforming value type instead of a subclass, which is the idiomatic replacement for the NullObject class. Extension-only members are statically dispatched, so any behaviour that real types must override belongs in the protocol declaration. Write an explicit struct or enum case when the degenerate state should be visible and pattern-matched; use Optional plus `??` when the caller must decide.
pitfalls: `??` converts absence into a default silently: apply it only where the default is domain-meaningful, otherwise the caller loses the chance to see a failure.
Value semantics: NoMetrics is copied on assignment, so it cannot hold shared state; if identity (===) matters, use a class singleton instead.
Protocol extension defaults are statically dispatched when called through the extension, so a real type cannot replace an extension-only implementation and the wrong body can win.

Optional chaining (delegate?.method()) is not the pattern: the object is still missing and the call is silently skipped, which is exactly the 'did this happen?' question the special case was meant to answer.
